nos_units.nos_title: Prepare for the Paragliding/Paramotoring/Paratrike Flight as
kus: KU1. SOPs, safety and service quality standards followed in the organization.
KU2. the company’s reporting structure and documentation procedures.
KU3. how to check connections and fittings of the canopy and identify faulty or damaged equipment.
KU4. techniques for assembling and dismantling the canopy wing.
KU5. the use of safety equipment in paragliding/paramotoring/paratrike like harness, helmet, personal flotation devices (PFD) if operating near a water body.
KU6. the use of two-way radios for communication.
KU7. how to recruit, assess and train the ground staff.
KU8. equipment maintenance and certifications.
KU9. appropriate clothing and accessories required for the activity.
KU10. basic maintenance and repair protocols for motors, propellers and machines .
KU11. process of equipment and service record logbook maintenance.
gs: GS1. plan and organize equipment checks on time.
GS3. be prompt, punctual and organized.

pcs.pc_description: access and assess daily work instructions and flight schedule from the organizer.
obtain and assess detailed information about the students’/clients’ age, gender, health issues(if any), special requests and past experience in paratrike/paramotoring/paragliding (if any).
access and assess information on launch and landing sites, weather and wind speeds.
ensure adequate trained ground staff is assigned for each activity based on the number of students/clients and assist the company/organizers to recruit new ground staff, if required.
assign and instruct existing ground staff on pre- flight tasks and specific roles and take responsibility for training all newly appointed ground staff.

ensure to check the certification of all equipment and conduct a visual inspection of all components of the wing such as panels, ribs, structural diagonals and straps, plastic rod sleeves, tabs, lines, splices, risers, seams, etc.
ensure to check the condition and numbers of all personal protective equipment like harness, carabiners and helmets carefully and have them ready before the students/clients arrive for the activity.
ensure to replace or repair all damaged equipment based on the manufacturer’s listed maintenance guidelines.
ensure to collect logs from the ground staff and maintain a master service record and log of any damaged equipment and hand over daily records to organizer.
supervise the ground staff to check all the connections and fittings before a flight.
ensure to check the fittings of all personal protective equipment worn by the students/clients and ensure they are wearing activity appropriate clothing.
use two-way radios and follow essential communication terms/signals to coordinate with the pilot/staff and instruct the ground staff on these protocols.
ensure all pre-flight tasks and responsibilities of self and team are conducted and completed on time.
ensure to record and document all testing and improvement of self-developed parts of a flying kit for paramotoring/paratrike.
offer help to persons with disabilities, when asked for.
empathize with and respect persons with disabilities.

nos_units.nos_title: Complete Post Flight Requirements as Ground Crew
kus: KU1. the manufacturer's recommended equipment maintenance policy.
KU2. proper methods of post activity equipment check and pack up.
KU3. company's documentation procedures including post trip equipment record logbook entries and equipment inspection recommendation.
KU4. the process for feedback exchange and documentation.
gs: GS1. writing equipment maintenance and service records.

modules.module_title: Inspect equipment and submit activity report

pcs.pc_description: ensure to check the condition of all equipment after the activity and supervise the ground staff.
ensure the ground staff carefully folds and packs the parachute/canopy as well as other equipment, collect and return the equipment to the organizer.
maintain a record of the total duration the canopy and equipment was used for, any damaged/faulty equipment, incidents, accidents or health related problems after the activity.
ensure to log the performance of each ground staff and provide daily written feedback to them and the organizer.

nos_units.nos_title: Assess and Mitigate Risks as Ground Crew
kus: KU1. organisational policies and procedures to enable safe response to an emergency situation according to one's own work role and level of responsibility.
KU2. contingency management techniques.
KU3. emergency protocols, call-out procedures and information to access emergency services personnel.
KU4. identifying damaged/faulty equipment and the equipment manufacturer's policy on maintenance and repair.
KU5. use of safety equipment, rescue techniques and basic first-aid methods.
KU6. how to recognize safety signs and symbols.
gs: GS1. communicate effectively with the students/clients/team.
GS3. be polite but firm with the students/clients without compromising safety.

modules.module_title: Ensure to take safety measures and respond to emergency situations

pcs.pc_description: brief the team and ground staff on the emergency action plan of the day and designate responsibility according to their role.
ensure that operation sites are protected and free from hazards or turbulence sources before starting the paragliding/paramotoring/paratrike activity.
ensure to keep the students/clients under observation and away from the operations area at all times.
ensure that each student/client is wearing a Personal Floatation Devices (PFD) and spares are attached to the flying equipment, when operating near water.

ensure that all the equipment being used is inspected/serviced annually including the line length, line breaking strength, porosity of the canopy, its tear strength and the motor used for paramotoring/paratrike.
ensure all damages reported in the daily maintenance logbook are repaired or replaced according to the manufacturer's specifications.
ensure to only use equipment, wing and reserve parachute certified by globally recognized organisations such as EN/SHV/DHV/AFNOR.
ensure that first-aid kits, stretchers (spinal board) are easily accessible on the site and provide basic first aid/CPR, if required.
ensure to have the radio communication devices operating both before and during the flight.
access and asses continuous weather reports and update the tandem pilot before and during the activity.
ensure to follow the organizer's prescribed emergency action plan and have all emergency teams, equipment and contacts of third party vendors for transportation at hand in case of an emergency.
establish communication and coordinate with the tandem pilot/organizer, ground crew team and all third party vendors to provide land and air rescue, in case of an emergency.
evacuate the students/clients from the danger zone and provide shelter till rescue arrives, in case of disasters.
ensure that food, water and other provisions are used judiciously till the rescue arrives.
maintain calm and be composed in emergency situations.
